text:
Emily Chen: Quick Q — I'm seeing odd behavior when combining stop sequences + max_tokens + nucleus sampling. Request had `max_tokens: 10`, `stop: ["\\n\\n"]`, `temperature: 0.9`, `top_p: 0.95`, `logprobs: 5`. The model returned text that appears to include 12 tokens (by our tokenizer) and the `logprobs` array is empty/null in the response. Anyone seen this?

Ryan Patel: Do you have exact request/response bodies? Are you hitting streaming or non-streaming? We had a regression where post-processing ran after streaming chunks got buffered.

Emily Chen: Non-streaming. Pasting a redacted example:```json
{
  "model": "redwood-alpha-1",
  "prompt": "Q: Write a short sign-off.\nA:",
  "max_tokens": 10,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.9,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "logprobs": 5
}
```Response (trimmed):```json
{
  "id": "resp-abc",
  "choices": [
    {
      "text": " Thanks! See you soon.\n\n",
      "logprobs": null
    }
  ]
}
```We counted tokens for the string (using our tokenizer): 12 tokens. We expected decoding to stop at the first stop sequence and to never exceed `max_tokens`. Also, requesting `logprobs` should return arrays — not null.

Ashley Gomez: Two separate things likely: (1) `max_tokens` is a hard limit on the decoder's output length, whereas `stop` is applied as post-processing — but if the decoder emits the stop tokens as part of the final sampled token, they can cause off-by-one counts depending on how you're counting tokens. (2) `logprobs` being null is concerning — should be returned whenever requested unless truncated for privacy/size reasons. Could be a codepath that strips `logprobs` for high-temperature sampling if we hit a fallback.

Matt: On the infra side, we enforce `max_tokens` at generation time (we stop sampling when the decoder has emitted N tokens). However, we append the stop sequence check after the final token selection pass. There's a known edge-case if the stop sequence spans multiple tokens and the sampler emits a partial match at the end; our post-cut may leave trailing bytes that your tokenizer counts as extra tokens. We should normalize by truncating to the stop substring before token counting in the API contract.

Ryan Patel: Re: `logprobs`: historically `logprobs` is generated by the same sampling path. If we run a faster approximate sampler for high `top_p`/high `temp` cases (we do a fast-approx path for performance), the approximate path did not populate the `logprobs` structure to save CPU. That needs to be fixed or documented in the contract.

Emily Chen: Reproduction steps I used: 1) POST to `/v1/completions` with the JSON above. 2) Non-streaming, no `user` header special casing. 3) Tokenize response with our tokenizer to verify counts. Observed: generated text includes `"\n\n"` (stop) but token count > max, and `logprobs` null.

Ashley Gomez: Proposed action items: - Clarify in API docs that `max_tokens` counts raw decode tokens and `stop` is applied as post-processing (we should add exact semantics for when stop matching crosses token boundaries). - Ensure `logprobs` contract: if `logprobs` requested, server must return per-token logprobs unless omitted for streaming partials or explicit truncation. - Add a unit test that exercises `stop` spanning multi-token boundaries with different tokenizers.

Matt: I'll open a backend PR to: 1) make post-processing truncation occur before emitting the final `text` and the token count field, 2) ensure the fast-approx sampling path also populates `logprobs` (or falls back to a slower path when `logprobs` requested). I'll link the PR in this thread.

deploy-bot: build/redwood-infer#1234 deployed to staging :rocket:

Emily Chen: Thanks — assigning this to @Matt for the infra fix. I also created a tiny repro test in the `eng-ml/tests` folder (link: gitlab.com/redwood/repro/stop-max-logprobs — redacted). Putting details there for QA.

Matt: Will run the repro on staging and post results here. ETA end of day.

Ryan Patel: Quick question — do we want to change the API contract (breaking) or just document the current behavior and fix the `logprobs` omission? If we change token counting semantics we should do an API-notice.

Ashley Gomez: Prefer documenting current behavior immediately and push a non-breaking clarification. If we change semantics (e.g., define `max_tokens` to mean "tokens after stop truncation"), that's a breaking change and needs a deprecation cycle.

Emily Chen: Agreed. For now doc + infra fix for `logprobs` would unblock my integration. If folks are OK I'll file a docs PR with the clarification and link it here.

Matt: 👍 I'll follow up with PR #567 (infra) and an integration test.

Ryan Patel: :thumbsup:

Ashley Gomez: Thanks, team.
